headline: Continued the 353 Wilder Street demolition application and named the Senior Planner interim administrator for 2026.
summary: The applicant for 353 Wilder Street plans to demolish part of a structure and build a new one in its place. That application was continued. Other actions included approving the July 13, 2026 minutes, approving 265 Dutton Street, Unit 8, and finding St. Michael's Church historically significant.
decisions: Continued the application for 353 Wilder Street (WSND-27-1) 7-0.
Approved the July 13, 2026 meeting minutes with the proposed edits 7-0.
Approved the Minor Development Review application for 265 Dutton Street, Unit 8, 7-0.
Determined St. Michael's Church historically significant to the City of Lowell and Centralville neighborhood, 7-0.
Agreed that staff can expedite the review and complete the permit administratively for the Merrimack Street violation matter.
Appointed the Senior Planner as Interim Historic Board Administrator for the remainder of 2026, 7-0.

plain_text:
LOWELL HISTORIC BOARD  
MINUTES  
Mayor’s Reception Room, Lowell City Hall  
September 14, 2026 at 6:00 p.m.  
  
Note: These minutes are not completed verbatim. For further detail, contact the Lowell Historic 
Board, Lowell City Hall, Room 51, 375 Merrimack Street or refer to video recordings available online 
at www.LTC.org.  
  
Members Present:  Chair George Villaras, Vice Chair Jeffrey Harris, Yovani Baez-Rose, Troy 
Depeiza, Aurora Erickson, Gray Fitzsimons, Lucia Walker  
         
Members Absent:  Member Deborah Belanger  
  
Others Present:  Dylan Ricker, Senior Planner  
  
The following represents the actions taken by the Historic Board at the 9/14/26 meeting.   
  
Chair Villaras called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.  
 
 
A quorum of the Board was present. Chair Villaras called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM 
 
I. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
A. WSND-27-1: 353 Wilder Street 
An application for a Historic Permit has been submitted by ASG Construction Corporation to 
demolish a portion of the existing structure at 353 Wilder Street. The applicant reports the 
portion of the existing structure is compromised. The applicant plans to construct a new 
structure in place of the demolished portion of the building. The property is located within the 
Wilder Street Neighborhood District, and requires a Major Development permit from the Lowell 
Historic Board for demolition of an existing structure. 
 
On Behalf: 
Brendan Conley, Applicant 
 
B. Conley explained the reasoning for the demolition, and the new rebuilding plan for the 
property. B. Conley said the existing building was not salvageable and they will maintain the 
same scale. B. Conley said the goal is to blend it into the historic district. 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion:
G. Fitzsimons noted the Board did not approve the demolition of the carriage house. B. Conley 
said they were following guidance from the previous administrator. 
 
J. Harris asked if the rebuild will be in the same footprint. B. Conley confirmed. J. Harris noted 
there are fewer gables that there were prior, but said there is one that plays into what was 
there before. J. Harris recommended removing the quoin bonding on the corners of the 
building. J. Harris said the standards are not meant to make historic references that make newer 
buildings appear old.  
 
J. Harris said the Wilder Street side of the addition should have more evenly spaced windows 
and doors, and said it currently has an awkward look. J. Harris recommended updates with 
windows to create more symmetry in the façade. B. Conley agreed. 
 
G. Villaras asked whether all of the roofing is being replaced. B. Conley said there is just new 
roofing for the addition and said the remaining building has a newer roof and the same material 
will be used.  
 
G. Fitzsimons recommended waiting to approve until viewing the updated design on the Wider 
Street façade. 
 
Motion: 
G. Fitzsimons motioned to continue the application, the motion was seconded by T. Depeiza. 
The motion pass unanimously, (7-0). 
 
II. MINUTES 
 
Approval of the July 13, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
 
G. Villaras said there some formatting issues that need to be fixed, but has no other comments. 
 
Y. Baez-Rose motioned to approve the meeting minutes with the proposed edits. G. Fitzsimons 
seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously, (7-0). 
 
III. OTHER BUSINESS 
 
A. Minor Development Review: 166 Suffolk Street 
 
On Behalf: 
Tristan Souza, Applicant’s Representative 
 
T. Souza said a concern was related to the proximity to the Western Canal and visibility to the 
street. T. Souza said she submitted revised plans, but said the number of panels were not able 
to be reduced based on the homeowner’s usage to keep solar feasible for the homeowner. 
 
Discussion: 
J. Harris said they appreciate the panels are more regular in size and more lienar. J. Harris said 
he wished there was more symmetry in the setback and noted the different setbacks of the 
panels. J. Harris said he prefers a minimum of a 2 ft setback to reduce the visibility from the
street. J. Harris asked if there is flexibility in how the panels can be positioned to meet a 2 ft 
setback to lessen visibility of the panels. 
 
T. Souza asked for clarity on the symmetry request and said her understanding is that the 30 
inch setback be located on each side. J. Harris said ideally there is at least a 2 ft setback. T. Souza 
they would like 36 inches, but there is some extra room on other roofs so that would be 
possible. T. Souza said they can offer the 2 ft setback, but will have to confirm with the engineer. 
T. Souza said they will add the setback and provide updated plans. J. Harris said after seeing 
plans the approval can be issued administratively. J. Harris added that the conduit coming down 
the side of the home should be painted to match the color of the building. T. Souza agreed. 
 
B. Informational Presentation: 41 Hurd Street 
 
This item was taken out of order first on the agenda. 
 
On Behalf: 
John Geary, Applicant’s Representative 
 
J. Geary said the applicant intends to seek a Major Development permit for the project. J. Geary 
explained the proposed project which includes demolishing the existing building and 
construction a new residential building. J. Geary explained the history of the courthouse site. J. 
Geary explained the submitted materials including documentation of the existing courthouse 
and an economic hardship letter. J. Geary said the applicant is seeking feedback on the archival 
report submitted, and feedback on the proposed redevelopment plan. J. Geary explained the 
RFP for the property. J. Geary said the applicant completed an analysis as to whether an 
adaptive reuse was possible, but the projected return was not large enough to get financing. 
 
Jeff Bush, Applicant 
 
J. Bush said Heritage Properties has completed other similar projects in the Downtown Lowell 
Historic District. J. Bush explained the past work of Heritage Properties on projects in historic 
districts. J. Bush said the most recent project was at 218 Middlesex Street. 
 
Aubrey Bennett, Applicant’s Architect 
 
A. Bennett said the elevations were designed to pay homage to the history of the site and were 
designed in reference to the courthouse. A. Bennett said the building was designed to connect 
to surrounding properties via materials such as red bricks which ties into the historic district. A. 
Bennett said the red brick is predominantly on the first floor to anchor the site. A. Bennett said a 
more contemporary fiber cement panel is used on upper floors. A. Bennett explained the 
window choices for the building. A. Bennett explained the elevations and surrounding 
properties. A. Bennett explained how the building interacts with the streetscape. A. Bennett said 
they are utilizing a rounded edge at the street corner. A. Bennett said the development bridges 
the multiple architectural styles of the street. 
 
Discussion: 
G. Fitzsimons said he is generally supportive of the design. G. Fitzsimons said his preference is 
rehab of historic buildings and asked how the ROI was calculated as well as total units. J. Bush
said they reviewed the site to see what could be built on the remaining land, and for ROI they 
reviewed the cost of development and income generated by the units. G. Fitzsimons asked if 
Market Square Architects did a rough design of keeping the courthouse. J. Bush said an informal 
review was done. G. Fitzsimons asked about the documentation of the building are up to historic 
standards. J. Bush said a form of documentation was submitted that does not meet HABS 
standards, and they are looking for clarification as to whether the submitted documentation is 
sufficient. 
 
J. Harris asked about the analysis for keeping the courthouse, and asked how many stories that 
would be. J. Bush explained how the analysis was done. J. Harris asked if the review took into 
account historic rehabilitation tax credits. J. Bush confirmed they took this into account, and 
said the new building would not get this benefit. J. Harris asked if they reviewed additions onto 
the existing structure. J. Bush said no, but conventional thought said the structure would not be 
viable. J. Harris said it is disappointing that no proposals were received that had rehab as an 
option. J. Harris said the building is a major historical element on this street. 
 
J. Harris asked if this was the only proposal received. Y. Baez-Rose confirmed. Y. Baez-Rose said 
the City coordinated with DCAMM. Y. Baez-Rose explained the RFP process and said ultimately 
only 1 proposal was received. Y. Baez-Rose said the disposition had to be explicit with the goal 
of housing. 
 
J. Harris said the photo documentation shows historic details in good condition on the interior 
and asked if they plan on incorporating these into the building. J. Bush recommended a tour of 
the building and said they are willing to incorporate these elements into the new building. 
 
A. Erickson said the Board knows the building poses significant challenges. A. Erickson said she is 
disappointed that elements of the façade were not incorporated into the design. A. Erickson 
said maintaining some elements would improve the historic continuity. A. Erickson noted that is 
a challenge to fit into the historic continuity given the different generations of buildings on the 
street. A. Erickson said she would like more info on how the building incorporates into the 
streetscape from additional locations. A. Erickson said she does not feel the rounded look fits 
into the area’s historic context. A. Erickson asked about the darker color used that is not used a 
lot in this area. A. Bennett said that was meant to help breakdown the scale, and help define the 
columns. 
 
G. Villaras noted the streetscape of Hurd Street around this site, and said if there is a way to use 
the wall to make it appear to be a remnant wall of the courthouse it would improve the 
streetscape and make the lot look less like parking lot. J. Harris said moving the parking further 
from the sidewalk would benefit the design of the project J, Bush said similar work was done at 
the 218 Middlesex Street project and they will look into adding this to the site in a way that 
preserves site lines. J. Bush said they will update plans to incorporate the recommendations. 
 
J. Geary said the applicant can arrange a site visit for Board members and will coordinate with 
staff. 
 
C. Minor Development Review: 15-19 Merrimack Street 
 
On Behalf:
None 
 
Discussion: 
None 
 
D. Minor Development Review: 265 Dutton Street, Unit 8 
 
On Behalf: 
Bradley Buitenhuys, Applicant’s Representative 
 
Discussion: 
The Board stated they had no concerns with the proposal. 
 
Motion: 
T. Depeiza motioned, and J. Harris seconded the motion to approve the application. The motion 
passed unanimously, (7-0). 
 
E. Historic Significance: St. Michael’s Church 
 
On Behalf: 
D. Ricker explained that the applicant is seeking a determination that the church is important to 
history, architecture, or culture of Lowell. D. Ricker said this is necessary for the property to be 
eligible for CPA Historic funds. 
 
Discussion: 
None 
 
Motion: 
J. Harris motioned to determine the property as historically significant to the City of Lowell and 
Centralville neighborhood. L. Walker seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously, (7-
0). 
 
F. Historic Board Violations: 295 Dutton Street, 65 Merrimack St, and 256 Merrimack Street 
 
On Behalf: 
D. Ricker explained each violation. D. Ricker said that he has had contact with 295 Dutton St, 
and 256 Merrimack St has since submitted an application for the work. 
 
Discussion: 
J. Harris said 256 Merrimack Street is also subject to a historic covenant from DCR. J. Harris 
provided context from DCR about the work. J. Harris said the all wood windows were deemed 
too expensive and instead were looking to use aluminum with wood faced over. J. Harris said 
after review they arrived at a solution S. Stowell was comfortable with. J. Harris said S. Stowell 
indicated to the Building Department the work was OK to proceed. J. Harris said DCR is satisfied 
with the design and said he is comfortable that the permit be issued by staff to expedite the 
process. J. Harris said the design is sensitive to the character of the building.
G. Fitzsimons clarified that J. Harris does not believe the final design needs to be vetter by the 
Board because S. Stowell has already reviewed it. J. Harris said given S. Stowell’s experience his 
review is sufficient. J. Harris recommended adding a tag on the building that it also requires DCR 
review. 
 
Y. Baez-Rose noted the Board requested review of how violations will be flagged. Y. Baez-Rose 
said the Building Department does neighborhood walks to check for violations, and a downtown 
walk was added to flag concerns downtown. Y. Baez-Rose noted when there are no files or 
emails related to prior review of properties it can be difficult to review. Y. Baez-Rose said the 
City will look into adding flags to properties requiring DCR review. 
 
J. Harris and Y. Baez-Rose agreed that staff can expedite the review and complete the permit 
administratively. 
 
G. Staff Update: Boott Mill Smokestack Lighting 
 
On Behalf: 
D. Ricker provided an update on the review of the minor development permit to light the Boott 
Mill smokestack. 
 
F. Faust said the smokestack will be list with LED lights by Lowell Waterways. 
 
Discussion: 
None 
 
H. Staff Updates: Sign Grants 
 
On Behalf: 
D. Ricker explained the program and that the materials were updated. 
 
Discussion: 
G. Villaras asked how the program is promoted. D. Ricker said it is promoted when we receive 
sign applications, and staff could work with the City Communications Team. Y. Baez-Rose added 
that the Economic Development Team promotes the program as well. Y. Baez-Rose noted past 
request for fee waivers, and said she is not comfortable with staff waiving fees. G. Villaras 
agreed with concerns regarding fee waivers, and recommended further discussion at the next 
meeting. A. Erickson asked why fees were being waived. Y. Baez-Rose said it is unclear and said 
we are unsure the total number of fees waived. 
 
J. Harris asked if other Boards have waivers. Y. Baez-Rose said the Board of Parks has fee waivers 
and explained their waiver process. Y. Baez-Rose said other land use boards do not waive fees, 
but there are a few waiver structures from other boards. 
 
I. Staff Update: Historic Tax Credit Letters of Support and FERC Letter 
 
On Behalf: 
D. Ricker explained the FERC and letters of support issued on behalf of the Historic Board.
Discussion: 
Y. Baez-Rose said a large cohort of stakeholders have been in contact about the FERC and a 
number of entities have been filing letters related to the FERC. Y. Baez-Rose nored each entity is 
filing their own letters. 
 
Peter Aucella said he works with the Lowell Waterways Vitality Initiative and said there was an 
opportunity to comment on FERC decision and noted he reached out to entities throughout 
Lowell. P. Aucella said right now the messaging is in support of the work of the City and Parks 
Service. P. Aucella said the goal is to ensure the community and NPS are involved in the process. 
P. Aucella said a goal is the canal management plan, and the current focus is on a deferred 
maintenance plan identified work to be done. G. Fitzsimons asked about a timeframe for further 
studies. P. Aucella said a Recreation Plan is supposed to be updated, a Historic Properties 
Maintenance Plan will be completed, and said the HPMP will involve the state Historic 
Preservation Agency. P. Aucella said they have not seen these plans yet. 
 
J. Staff Update: Historic Home Markers 
 
On Behalf: 
D. Ricker explained the historic home markers program history. 
 
Discussion: 
G. Villaras asked how the program would work, and requested more info to insure the program 
would be self-sustaining. 
 
A. Erickson asked if it could be done for homes not located within the historic districts with 
historic significance. 
 
K. Discussion: Charles D. Palmer Portrait Restoration 
 
This item was taken out of order second on the agenda. 
 
On Behalf: 
Erik Gitschier 
 
E. Gitschier said Charles D Palmer was the Mayor in 1888-1890 when the City Hall property was 
purchased. E. Gitschier said he would like to recognize his significance to getting City Hall and 
Memorial Hall built. E. Gitschier said they would like to represent this Mayor like the other 
Mayors and restore the portrait to a 2x2 size of the other portraits. 
 
Discussion: 
A. Erickson said the proposal seems appropriate. 
 
Y. Baez-Rose said there is funding the Board receives that can be used for this project if the 
Board feels it is appropriate. Y. Baez-Rose said staff can do research to understand the total cost 
of the work. J. Harris asked if it is the expectation that the Board fully fund the work. E. Gitschier 
said the goal is for the Board to fully fund the project. J. Harris asked if the plan was to do a high 
level scan to create the larger portrait. Y. Baez-Rose said that is possible and part of the work is
to determine what options will work to ensure the picture is not blurry. E. Gitschier said a 
number of portraits in the Mayors Reception Room was done this way. 
 
G. Fitzsimons asked if it was considered to consult with the Lowell High History Department. E. 
Gitschier said they work with S. Stowell in the past. 
 
J. Harris said he was no objections to looking to getting the portrait size increased. 
 
L. Historic Board Administrator: Discussion and Vote 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
Peter Aucella, 30 Parkview Avenue 
 
P. Aucella said the City advocated for the creation of the National park, and Senator Tsongas 
added a condition requiring design controls through a Historic Board to ensure design controls 
would be in place with federal funding. P. Aucella said it was preferred to create a local Board to 
review the projects in Lowell. P. Aucella said the administrator should have expertise in historic 
preservation. P. Aucella said the Board has operated without major controversy. P. Aucella said 
the Board should have its own dedicated administrator.  
 
Fred Faust  
 
F. Faust explained the history of the creation of the National Park. F. Faust said historical 
expertise is important to the Historic Board Administrator position. F. Faust said the 
administrator should be an expert in the field and that the Historic Board is the appointing 
authority.  
 
Discussion: 
G. Villaras said if there are any direct questions they can ask the City Solicitor who is present. G. 
Villaras asked if there must be 1 specific administrator or can the City lay out an administration 
process. C. Williams said the legislation does not speak to requiring 1 individual specifically, C. 
Williams said the Board could allow multiple people to perform the duties. G. Fitzsimons said he 
believes the legislation means there is 1 Historic Board Administrator appointed by the Board. C. 
Williams noted tissues with reading the legislation literally. C. Williams said he believes if the 
intent was to be only help by 1 person it would say that, and it does not. 
 
A. Erickson requested the specific passage be read aloud. C. Williams read the referenced 
section aloud. G. Fitzsimons said the legislation cites one administrator. C. Williams there are no 
rules and regulations for the Board.  
 
G. Fitzsimons asked the process for advertising the role. Y. Baez-Rose said the role costs money, 
and requested the following paragraph be read stating the administrator is an employee of the 
City of Lowell. Y. Baez-Rose said the budget process was difficult, and tough decisions had to be 
made. Y. Baez-Rose said DPD presented a plan to continue the administrative work of the Board. 
Y. Baez-Rose said the position still exists, but there is no money for the position. Y. Baez-Rose
said if money is found they would love to fill the position. Y. Baez-Rose said the Board would be 
able to pay for the position and cannot require the City to hire the role. Y. Baez-Rose noted 
everywhere in DPD saw a cut. Y. Baez-Rose said DPD provided a plan, and any suggested 
changes need to be based in the reality of the financial constraints that exist. 
 
G. Fitzsimons said the City felt in the past the position was a valued position, and asked how the 
position was passed to different administrators. G. Fitzsimons asked if there is any other funding 
available. Y. Baez-Rose said the position has historically been housed in DPD, but in the past the 
position was not entirely funded by the City, it was at one point a shared expense. Y. Baez-Rose 
said initially it was shared, and added there was an assistant at one point as well. Y. Baez-Rose 
said every Department had cuts and staff reductions. Y. Baez-Rose said the Board has funding 
and at last check there was roughly $100,000, but that has accumulated over time and it is not 
an annual revenue generator. Y. Baez-Rose added this funding funds different Board programs. 
Y. Baez-Rose said the Board does not generate enough funding to fund the position. 
 
A. Erickson said it is the Board’s obligation to appoint an administrator and asked if they must be 
full time. Y. Baez-Rose said this is not required, but the position is a union position. C. Williams 
said there would have to be negotiation with the union to reduce the position to part time. A. 
Erickson asked if they could appoint a volunteer administrator. C. Williams said this would 
require negotiation with the union. A. Erickson asked if the position could be grant funded. C. 
Williams said as long as funds came into the City that would be doable. Y. Baez-Rose said DPD 
has positions that are grant funded, and noted some of these positions had to be cut due to loss 
of grant funding. C. Williams said this would also need to be negotiated with the union. 
 
G. Villaras asked if there is an immediate need to appoint an administrator or if they can 
continue to operate in the current dynamic. C. Williams said he would defer to the Board’s 
judgement is appropriate. Y. Baez-Rose said she would be concerned from a staff perspective 
and said the Board would need to be comfortable without the administrative work getting done. 
J. Harris said letters and decisions have been issued in the meantime. Y. Baez-Rose said the 
Board has been working toward a solution, and said if the Board is not comfortable moving 
forward with that plan then staff should not need to act in that capacity.  
 
A. Erickson asked if it could be an interim administrator and be revoted each month. G. 
Fitzsimons said the Board should appoint 1 administrator and it should be the Senior Planner. G. 
Fitzsimons defined interim as until funding is available for the position to be filled. Y. Baez-Rose 
said there needs to be a shorter timeframe if interim. Y. Baez-Rose recommended a calendar 
year. Y. Baez-Rose recommended 1 month. 
 
Motion: 
G. Fitzsimons motioned to have the Senior Planner serve as the Interim Historic Board 
Administrator for the remained of 2026. Y. Baez-Rose seconded the motion. The motion passed 
unanimously, (7-0). 
 
M. Board Member Items/Inquiries 
 
Discussion:
Y. Baez-Rose noted there has been no one able to fill the BAR position on the Board. G. Villaras 
said S. Stowell had been contacting people about the vacancy. The Board said they would work 
together to appoint a member. 
 
IV. Adjournment 
 
G. Fitzsimons motioned to adjourn. L. Walker seconded. The motion passed unanimously, (7-0). The 
meeting was adjourned at 8:26 PM.
